title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 77 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 462–464 (Night 77, continuing directly from nights-76), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 77 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. The chamberlain of Sharkān, who has married Nuzhat al-Zamān, learns from the vizier Dandān of the old king’s death and the nobles’ choice of Ḍawʾ al-Makān; the emirs consult, the chamberlain rides ahead to prepare the camp, tells the two siblings the news, and urges Ḍawʾ al-Makān to accept the throne of Baghdad while his brother Sharkān keeps Damascus. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ السَّابِعَةُ وَالسَّبْعُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-sābiʿatu wa-al-sabʿūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the seventh and the seventy,
sentences.i: And when it was the seventy-seventh night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدَأَنَّ حَاجِبَ شَرْكَانَ لَمَّا سَمِعَ مِنَ الْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ مَا ذَكَرَهُ مِنْ خَبَرِ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ تَأَسَّفَ وَلَكِنَّهُ فَرِحَ لِزَوْجَتِهِ وَأَخِيهَا ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ لِأَنَّهُ يَصِيرُ سُلْطَاناً بِبَغْدَادَ مَكَانَ أَبِيهِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīda anna ḥājiba sharkāna lammā samiʿa mina al-wazīri dandāna mā dhakarahu min khabari al-maliki ʿumara bni al-nuʿmāni taʾassafa wa-lākinnahu fariḥa li-zawjatihi wa-akhīhā ḍawʾi al-makāni li-annahu yaṣīru sulṭānan bi-baghdāda makāna abīhi
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that the chamberlain of Sharkān, when he heard from the vizier Dandān what he had mentioned of the news of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, was sorry; but he rejoiced for his wife and her brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān, because he would become sultan in Baghdad in the place of his father.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when Sharkān’s chamberlain heard from the vizier Dandān the news of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, he grieved; yet he rejoiced for his wife and her brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān, since Ḍawʾ al-Makān would become sultan in Baghdad in his father’s place.
sentences.n: The print runs أن into the word before it (السعيدان, “the happy — that”); it is read as two words. The one who “would become sultan” is Ḍawʾ al-Makān, not the chamberlain.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ الْتَفَتَ الْحَاجِبُ إِلَى الْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ وَقَالَ إِنَّ قِصَّتَكُمْ مِنْ أَعْجَبِ الْعَجَائِبِ
sentences.tr: thumma iltafata al-ḥājibu ilā al-wazīri dandāna wa-qāla inna qiṣṣatakum min aʿjabi al-ʿajāʾibi
sentences.l: Then the chamberlain turned to the vizier Dandān and said: Truly, your story is from the most wondrous of the wonders.
sentences.i: Then the chamberlain turned to the vizier Dandān and said, “Yours is among the most marvellous of tales.”

sentences.t: اِعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْوَزِيرُ الْكَبِيرُ إِنَّكُمْ حَيْثُ صَادَفْتُمُونِي الْآنَ أَرَاحَكُمُ اللَّهُ مِنَ التَّعَبِ وَقَدْ جَاءَكُمُ الْأَمْرَكَمَا تَشْتَهُونَ عَلَى أَهْوَنِ سَبَبٍ لِأَنَّ اللَّهَ رَدَّ إِلَيْكُمْ ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ هُوَ وَأُخْتَهُ نُزْهَةَالزَّمَانِ وَانْصَلَحَ الْأَمْرُ وَهَانَ
sentences.tr: iʿlam ayyuhā al-wazīru al-kabīru innakum ḥaythu ṣādaftumūnī al-āna arāḥakumu allāhu mina al-taʿabi wa-qad jāʾakumu al-amra ka-mā tashtahūna ʿalā ahwani sababin li-anna allāha radda ilaykum ḍawʾa al-makāni huwa wa-ukhtahu nuzhata al-zamāni wa-inṣalaḥa al-amru wa-hāna
sentences.l: Know, O vizier the great, that inasmuch as you have chanced upon me now, God give-you-rest from the weariness, the affair has come to you as you desire, upon the easiest cause: for God has returned to you Ḍawʾ al-Makān, he and his sister Nuzhat al-Zamān; and the affair has been set right and has grown easy.
sentences.i: Know, great vizier, that in meeting me now you have found rest from your weariness: matters have come to you just as you wish, by the easiest of means. For God has restored to you Ḍawʾ al-Makān and his sister Nuzhat al-Zamān; the affair is mended and made light.
sentences.n: The print runs الأمر and كما into one word (الامركما), and the two names نزهة الزمان and ضوء المكان are sometimes written as single words; each is read as two.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْوَزِيرُ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ فَرِحَ فَرَحاً شَدِيداً ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ أَيُّهَا الْحَاجِبُ أَخْبِرْنِي بِقِصَّتِهِمَا وَبِمَا جَرَى لَهُمَا وَبِسَبَبِ غِيَابِهِمَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-wazīru hādhā al-kalāma fariḥa faraḥan shadīdan thumma qāla lahu ayyuhā al-ḥājibu akhbirnī bi-qiṣṣatihimā wa-bi-mā jarā lahumā wa-bi-sababi ghiyābihimā
sentences.l: And when the vizier heard this speech he rejoiced a violent joy; then he said to him: O chamberlain, inform me of their two story, and of what flowed to the two of them, and of the cause of their two absence.
sentences.i: When the vizier heard this he was overjoyed, and said to him, “Chamberlain, tell me their story: what befell them, and why they were gone.”

sentences.t: فَحَدَّثَهُ بِحَدِيثِ نُزْهَةِ الزَّمَانِ وَأَنَّهَا صَارَتْ زَوْجَتَهُ وَأَخْبَرَهُ بِحَدِيثِ ضَوْءِالْمَكَانِ مِنْ أَوَّلِهِ إِلَى آخِرِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ḥaddathahu bi-ḥadīthi nuzhati al-zamāni wa-annahā ṣārat zawjatahu wa-akhbarahu bi-ḥadīthi ḍawʾi al-makāni min awwalihi ilā ākhirihi
sentences.l: So he related to him the account of Nuzhat al-Zamān, and that she had become his wife, and informed him of the account of Ḍawʾ al-Makān from its first to its last.
sentences.i: So he told him Nuzhat al-Zamān’s story, and how she had become his wife, and told him Ḍawʾ al-Makān’s story from beginning to end.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ الْحَاجِبُ مِنْ حَدِيثِهِ أَرْسَلَ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ إِلَى الْأُمَرَاءِ وَالْوُزَرَاءِ وَأَكَابِرِ الدَّوْلَةِ وَأَطْلَعَهُمْ عَلَى الْقِصَّةِ فَفَرِحُوا بِذَلِكَ فَرَحاً شَدِيداً وَتَعَجَّبُوا مِنْ هَذَا الِاتِّفَاقِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha al-ḥājibu min ḥadīthihi arsala al-wazīru dandānu ilā al-umarāʾi wa-al-wuzarāʾi wa-akābiri al-dawlati wa-aṭlaʿahum ʿalā al-qiṣṣati fa-fariḥū bi-dhālika faraḥan shadīdan wa-taʿajjabū min hādhā al-ittifāqi
sentences.l: And when the chamberlain finished his account, the vizier Dandān sent to the emirs and the viziers and the great-ones of the state, and made them aware of the story; and they rejoiced at that a violent joy, and marvelled at this coincidence.
sentences.i: When the chamberlain had finished his account, the vizier Dandān sent for the emirs, the viziers and the great men of the state, and told them the story. They were overjoyed, and marvelled at such a coincidence.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ اجْتَمَعُوا كُلُّهُمْ وَجَاؤُا عِنْدَ الْحَاجِبِ وَوَقَفُوا فِي خِدْمَتِهِ وَقَبَّلُوا الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَأَقْبَلَ الْوَزِيرُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ الْوَقْتِ عَلَى الْحَاجِبِ وَوَقَفَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr: thumma ijtamaʿū kulluhum wa-jāʾū ʿinda al-ḥājibi wa-waqafū fī khidmatihi wa-qabbalū al-arḍa bayna yadayhi wa-aqbala al-wazīru min dhālika al-waqti ʿalā al-ḥājibi wa-waqafa bayna yadayhi
sentences.l: Then they gathered, all of them, and came to the chamberlain, and stood in his service, and kissed the earth between his two hands; and the vizier, from that time, turned-toward the chamberlain and stood between his two hands.
sentences.i: Then they all gathered, came to the chamberlain, stood in his service and kissed the ground before him; and from that moment the vizier turned his attention to the chamberlain and stood in his presence.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْحَاجِبَ عَمِلَ فِى ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ دِ يوَاناً عَظِيماً وَجَلَسَ هُوَ وَالْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ عَلَى تَخْتٍ وَبَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمَا جَمِيعُ الْأُمَرَاءِ وَالْكُبَرَاءِ وَأَرْبَابِ الْمَنَاصِبِ عَلَى حَسَبِ مَرَاتِبِهِمْ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-ḥājiba ʿamila fī dhālika al-yawmi dīwānan ʿaẓīman wa-jalasa huwa wa-al-wazīru dandānu ʿalā takhtin wa-bayna aydīhimā jamīʿu al-umarāʾi wa-al-kubarāʾi wa-arbābi al-manāṣibi ʿalā ḥasabi marātibihim
sentences.l: Then the chamberlain made, on that day, a great divan, and he sat, he and the vizier Dandān, upon a throne, and between their two hands all the emirs and the grandees and the holders-of-offices, according to their ranks.
sentences.i: Then, that same day, the chamberlain held a great audience, and sat with the vizier Dandān on a throne, while all the emirs, grandees and office-holders were ranged before them, each according to his rank.
sentences.n: The print splits دِيوَاناً (“divan”, a formal audience) into د يوانا; it is read as one word.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَلُّوا السُّكَّرَ فِي مَاءِ الْوَرْدِ وَشَرِبُوا
sentences.tr: thumma ballū al-sukkara fī māʾi al-wardi wa-sharibū
sentences.l: Then they moistened the sugar in the water of the rose, and drank.
sentences.i: Then they dissolved sugar in rosewater and drank.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَعَدَ الْأُمَرَاءُ لِلْمَشُورَةِ وَأَعْطَوْا بَقِيَّةَ الْجَيْشِ إِذْناً فِي أَنْ يَرْكَبُوا مَعَ بَعْضِهِمْ وَيَتَقَدَّمُوا قَلِيلاً قَلِيلاً حَتَّى يُتِمُّوا الْمَشُورَةَ وَيَلْحَقُوهُمْ
sentences.tr: thumma qaʿada al-umarāʾu li-al-mashūrati wa-aʿṭaw baqiyyata al-jayshi idhnan fī an yarkabū maʿa baʿḍihim wa-yataqaddamū qalīlan qalīlan ḥattā yutimmū al-mashūrata wa-yalḥaqūhum
sentences.l: Then the emirs sat for the consultation, and gave the rest of the army leave to ride together and to advance little by little until they should complete the consultation and overtake them.
sentences.i: Then the emirs sat down to take counsel, and gave the rest of the army leave to mount together and go forward a little at a time, until the council was done and the emirs could overtake them.
sentences.n: The print puts the shadda of يتّموا on the ت; it is read yutimmū, “they complete”, with the doubling on the م.

sentences.t: فَقَبَّلُوا الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَى الْحَاجِبِ وَرَكِبُوا وَقُدَّامَهُمْ رَايَاتُ الْحَرْبِ
sentences.tr: fa-qabbalū al-arḍa bayna yaday al-ḥājibi wa-rakibū wa-quddāmahum rāyātu al-ḥarbi
sentences.l: And they kissed the earth between the two hands of the chamberlain, and rode, and in front of them the banners of war.
sentences.i: The troops kissed the ground before the chamberlain and rode off, the banners of war carried before them.
sentences.n: Here “they” are the army, who ride ahead; the emirs follow in the next sentence.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ الْكُبَرَاءُ مِنْ مَشُورَتِهِمْ رَكِبُوا وَلَحِقُوا الْعَسَاكِرَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha al-kubarāʾu min mashūratihim rakibū wa-laḥiqū al-ʿasākira
sentences.l: And when the grandees had finished from their consultation, they rode and overtook the armies.
sentences.i: When the grandees had finished their council, they rode and caught up with the troops.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَقْبَلَ الْحَاجِبُ عَلَى الْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ وَقَالَ لَهُ الرَّأْيُ عِنْدِي أَنْ أَتَقَدَّمَ وَأَسْبِقَكُمْ لِأَجْلِ أَنْ أُهَيِّءَ لِلسُّلْطَانِ مَكَاناً يُنَاسِبُهُ وَأُعْلِمَهُ بِقُدُومِكُمْ وَإِنَّكُمُ اخْتَرْتُمُوهُ عَلَى أَخِيهِ شَرْكَانَ سُلْطَاناً عَلَيْكُمْ
sentences.tr: thumma aqbala al-ḥājibu ʿalā al-wazīri dandāna wa-qāla lahu al-raʾyu ʿindī an ataqaddama wa-asbiqakum li-ajli an uhayyiʾa li-al-sulṭāni makānan yunāsibuhu wa-uʿlimahu bi-qudūmikum wa-innakumu ikhtartumūhu ʿalā akhīhi sharkāna sulṭānan ʿalaykum
sentences.l: Then the chamberlain turned to the vizier Dandān and said to him: The opinion with me is that I go ahead and precede you, for the sake of preparing for the sultan a place that suits him, and informing him of your coming, and that you have chosen him over his brother Sharkān as sultan over you.
sentences.i: Then the chamberlain turned to the vizier Dandān and said, “My counsel is that I go ahead of you and prepare a fitting place for the sultan, and tell him of your coming, and that you have chosen him as your sultan in preference to his brother Sharkān.”

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْوَزِيرُ نِعْمَ الرَّأْيُ الَّذِي رَأَيْتَهُ ثُمَّ نَهَضَ وَنَهَضَ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ تَعْظِيماً لَهُ وَقَدَّمَ لَهُ التَّقَادِمَ وَأَقْسَمَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَقْبَلَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-wazīru niʿma al-raʾyu alladhī raʾaytahu thumma nahaḍa wa-nahaḍa al-wazīru dandānu taʿẓīman lahu wa-qaddama lahu al-taqādima wa-aqsama ʿalayhi an yaqbalahā
sentences.l: And the vizier said: Excellent is the opinion that you have seen. Then he rose, and the vizier Dandān rose, in honouring of him, and presented to him the gifts, and swore upon him that he accept them.
sentences.i: The vizier said, “Excellent is the counsel you have given.” Then the chamberlain rose, and the vizier Dandān rose too, in honour of him; he offered him gifts and swore that he must accept them.
sentences.n: The print reads رايته (“you saw”), as it were “the counsel you have seen”, i.e. judged best.

sentences.t: وَكَذَلِكَ الْأُمَرَاءُ الْكِبَارُ وَأَرْبَابُ الْمَنَاصِبِ قَدَّمُوا لَهُ التَّقَادِمَ وَدَعَوْا لَهُ وَقَالُوا لَهُ لَعَلَّكَ تُحَدِّثُ السُّلْطَانَ ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ فِي أَمْرِنَا لِيُبْقِيَنَا مُسْتَمِرِّينَ فِي مَنَاصِبِنَا فَأَجَا بَهُمْ لَمَّا سَأَلُوهُ
sentences.tr: wa-kadhālika al-umarāʾu al-kibāru wa-arbābu al-manāṣibi qaddamū lahu al-taqādima wa-daʿaw lahu wa-qālū lahu laʿallaka tuḥaddithu al-sulṭāna ḍawʾa al-makāni fī amrinā li-yubqiyanā mustamirrīna fī manāṣibinā fa-ajā bahum lammā saʾalūhu
sentences.l: And likewise the emirs the great and the holders-of-offices presented to him the gifts and prayed for him, and said to him: Perhaps you will speak to the sultan Ḍawʾ al-Makān about our affair, that he keep us continuing in our offices. And he answered them when they asked him.
sentences.i: The senior emirs and the office-holders did likewise: they offered him gifts and prayed for him, and said, “Perhaps you will speak to Sultan Ḍawʾ al-Makān on our behalf, that he may keep us in our posts.” And he answered them as they asked.
sentences.n: The print divides فأجابهم (“and he answered them”) as فاجا بهم; it is read as one word.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَمَرَ غِلْمَانَهُ بِالسَّيْرِ فَأَرْسَلَ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ الْخِيَامَ مَعَ الْحَاجِبِ وَأَمَرَ الْفَرَّاشِينَ أَنْ يَنْصِبُوهَا خَارِجَ الْمَدِينَةِ بِمَسَافَةِ يَوْمٍ فَامْتَثَلُوا أَمْرَهُ
sentences.tr: thumma amara ghilmānahu bi-al-sayri fa-arsala al-wazīru dandānu al-khiyāma maʿa al-ḥājibi wa-amara al-farrāshīna an yanṣibūhā khārija al-madīnati bi-masāfati yawmin fa-imtathalū amrahu
sentences.l: Then he ordered his servants to the going, and the vizier Dandān sent the tents with the chamberlain and ordered the tent-pitchers to pitch them outside the city at a distance of a day; and they complied with his command.
sentences.i: Then he ordered his servants to set out, and the vizier Dandān sent tents along with the chamberlain, and ordered the tent-pitchers to set them up a day’s journey outside the city; and they did as he commanded.

sentences.t: وَرَكِبَ الْحَاجِبُ وَهُوَ فِي غَايَةِ الْفَرَحِ وَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ مَا أَبْرَكَ هَذِهِ السَّفْرَةَ وَعَظُمَتْ زَوْجَتُهُ فِي عَيْنِهِ وَكَذَلِكَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-rakiba al-ḥājibu wa-huwa fī ghāyati al-faraḥi wa-qāla fī nafsihi mā abraka hādhihi al-safrata wa-ʿaẓumat zawjatuhu fī ʿaynihi wa-kadhālika ḍawʾu al-makāni
sentences.l: And the chamberlain rode, and he at the utmost of joy, and said in his self: How blessed is this journey! And his wife grew great in his eye, and likewise Ḍawʾ al-Makān.
sentences.i: The chamberlain rode off, in the height of joy, and said to himself, “How blessed this journey is!” His wife had grown great in his eyes, and so had Ḍawʾ al-Makān.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ جَدَّ فِى السَّفَرِ إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلَ إِلَى مَكَانٍ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ الْمَدِينَةِ مَسَافَةُ يَوْمٍ ثُمَّ أَمَرَ بِالنُّزُولِ فِيهِ لِأَجْلِ الرَّاحَةِ وَتَهْيِئَةِ مَكَانٍ لِجُلُوسِ السُّلْطَانِ ضَوْءِالْمَكَانِ بْنِ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
sentences.tr: thumma jadda fī al-safari ilā an waṣala ilā makānin baynahu wa-bayna al-madīnati masāfatu yawmin thumma amara bi-al-nuzūli fīhi li-ajli al-rāḥati wa-tahyiʾati makānin li-julūsi al-sulṭāni ḍawʾi al-makāni bni al-maliki ʿumara bni al-nuʿmāni
sentences.l: Then he exerted himself in the travelling until he arrived at a place between it and the city the distance of a day; then he ordered the alighting in it, for the sake of rest and the preparing of a place for the sitting of the sultan Ḍawʾ al-Makān son of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān.
sentences.i: Then he pressed on with the journey until he reached a place a day’s distance from the city, and there he ordered a halt, for rest and to make ready a place for the sultan Ḍawʾ al-Makān, son of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, to sit.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَزَلَ مِنْ بَعِيدٍ هُوَ وَمَمَا لِيكِهِ وَأَمَرَ الْخُدَّامَ أَنْ يَسْتَأْذِنُوا السَّيِّدَةَ نُزْهَةَالزَّمَانِ فِي أَنْ يَدْخُلَ عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: thumma nazala min baʿīdin huwa wa-mamālīkihi wa-amara al-khuddāma an yastaʾdhinū al-sayyidata nuzhata al-zamāni fī an yadkhula ʿalayhā
sentences.l: Then he alighted at a distance, he and his mamluks, and ordered the servants to ask leave of the lady Nuzhat al-Zamān for him to enter upon her.
sentences.i: Then he dismounted at a distance, with his mamluks, and told the servants to ask the lady Nuzhat al-Zamān’s leave for him to come in to her.
sentences.n: The print divides ومماليكه (“and his mamluks”, his slave-soldiers) as ومما ليكه; it is read as one word.

sentences.t: فَاسْتَأْذَنُوهَا فِي شَأْنِ ذَلِكَ فَأَذِنَتْ لَهُ فَدَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا وَاجْتَمَعَ بِهَا وَبِأَخِيهَا
sentences.tr: fa-istaʾdhanūhā fī shaʾni dhālika fa-adhinat lahu fa-dakhala ʿalayhā wa-ijtamaʿa bihā wa-bi-akhīhā
sentences.l: So they asked her leave in the matter of that, and she gave leave to him, and he entered upon her and met with her and with her brother.
sentences.i: They asked her leave about this, and she granted it; so he went in to her and met with her and with her brother.

sentences.t: وَأَخْبَرَهُمَا بِمَوْتِ أَبِيهِمَا وَأَنَّ ضَوْءَالْمَكَانِ جَعَلَهُ الرُّؤَسَاءُ مَلِكاً عَلَيْهِمْ عِوَضاً عَنْ أَبِيهِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ وَهَنَّا هُمَا بِالْمُلْكِ فَبَكَيَا عَلَى فَقْدِ أَبِيهِمَا وَسَأَلَا عَنْ سَبَبِ قَتْلِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-akhbarahumā bi-mawti abīhimā wa-anna ḍawʾa al-makāni jaʿalahu al-ruʾasāʾu malikan ʿalayhim ʿiwaḍan ʿan abīhi ʿumara bni al-nuʿmāni wa-hannaʾahumā bi-al-mulki fa-bakayā ʿalā faqdi abīhimā wa-saʾalā ʿan sababi qatlihi
sentences.l: And he informed the two of them of the death of their father, and that the chiefs had made Ḍawʾ al-Makān king over them in place of his father ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān; and he congratulated the two of them on the kingship, and they wept for the loss of their father, and asked about the cause of his killing.
sentences.i: He told them of their father’s death, and that the chiefs had made Ḍawʾ al-Makān king over them in place of his father ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. He congratulated them on the kingship, and they wept for the loss of their father and asked how he had been killed.
sentences.n: The print divides وهنّاهما (“and he congratulated them both”) as وهنّا هما; it is read as one word.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُمَا الْخَبَرُ مَعَ الْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ وَفِي غَدٍ يَكُونُ هُوَ وَالْجَيْشُ كُلُّهُ فِي هَذَا الْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahumā al-khabaru maʿa al-wazīri dandāna wa-fī ghadin yakūnu huwa wa-al-jayshu kulluhu fī hādhā al-makāni
sentences.l: And he said to the two of them: The news is with the vizier Dandān, and tomorrow he will be, he and the army all of it, in this place.
sentences.i: Then he said to them, “The whole account is with the vizier Dandān, and tomorrow he and the entire army will be in this place.”

sentences.t: وَمَا بَقِيَ فِى الْأَمْرِ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ إِلَّا أَنْ تَفْعَلَ مَا أَشَارُوا بِهِ لِأَنَّهُمْ كُلَّهُمُ اخْتَارُوكَ سُلْطَاناً وَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلْ سَلْطَنُوا غَيْرَكَ وَأَنْتَ لَا تَأْمَنُ عَلَى نَفْسِكَ مِنَ الَّذِي يَتَسَلْطَنُ غَيْرَكَ فَرُبَّمَا يَقْتُلُكَ أَوْ يَقَعُ الْفَشَلُ بَيْنَكُمَا وَيَخْرُجُ الْمُلْكُ مِنْ أَيْدِيكُمَا
sentences.tr: wa-mā baqiya fī al-amri ayyuhā al-maliku illā an tafʿala mā ashārū bihi li-annahum kullahumu ikhtārūka sulṭānan wa-in lam tafʿal salṭanū ghayraka wa-anta lā taʾmanu ʿalā nafsika mina alladhī yatasalṭanu ghayraka fa-rubbamā yaqtuluka aw yaqaʿu al-fashalu baynakumā wa-yakhruju al-mulku min aydīkumā
sentences.l: And nothing remains in the affair, O king, except that you do what they have indicated, because they all have chosen you as sultan; and if you do not, they will make-sultan another than you, and you are not safe for yourself from the one who becomes-sultan other than you; for perhaps he will kill you, or failure will fall between the two of you, and the kingdom will go out from your two hands.
sentences.i: Nothing remains, O king, but for you to do what they have asked: they have all chosen you as sultan, and if you refuse they will set up another, and you cannot feel safe from whoever is made sultan in your place. He might kill you, or discord might arise between you, and the kingdom would slip from your hands.
sentences.n: سَلْطَنُوا and يَتَسَلْطَنُ are verbs made from سلطان (“sultan”): “to install as sultan” and “to rule as sultan”. They are colloquial formations, not Classical. The “you” of بينكما and أيديكما is the dual: Ḍawʾ al-Makān and his sister.

sentences.t: فَأَطْرَقَ بِرَأْسِهِ سَاعَةً مِنَ الزَّمَانِ ثُمَّ قَالَ قَبِلْتُ هَذَا الْأَمْرَ لِأَنَّهُ لَا يُمْكِنُ التَّخَلِّي عَنْهُ وَتَحَقَّقَ أَنَّ الْحَاجِبَ تَكَلَّمَ بِمَا فِيهِ الرَّشَادُ
sentences.tr: fa-aṭraqa bi-raʾsihi sāʿatan mina al-zamāni thumma qāla qabiltu hādhā al-amra li-annahu lā yumkinu al-takhallī ʿanhu wa-taḥaqqaqa anna al-ḥājiba takallama bi-mā fīhi al-rashādu
sentences.l: And he bowed with his head an hour of the time, then said: I have accepted this affair, because it is not possible to relinquish it; and he was certain that the chamberlain had spoken with what has in it right-guidance.
sentences.i: He bowed his head for a while, then said, “I accept this, since it cannot be refused,” and he saw clearly that the chamberlain had spoken wisely.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ لِلْحَاجِبِ يَا عَمِّ وَكَيْفَ أَعْمَلُ مَعَ أَخِي شَرْكَانَ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla li-al-ḥājibi yā ʿammi wa-kayfa aʿmalu maʿa akhī sharkāna
sentences.l: Then he said to the chamberlain: O uncle, and how shall I act with my brother Sharkān?
sentences.i: Then he said to the chamberlain, “Uncle, and what shall I do about my brother Sharkān?”
sentences.n: يا عمّ, “O uncle”, is a respectful form of address to an older man, not a statement of kinship.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا وَلَدِي أَخُوكَ يَكُونُ سُلْطَانَ دِمَشْقَ وَأَنْتَ سُلْطَانُ بَغْدَادَ فَشُدَّ عَزْمَكَ وَجَهِّزْ أَمْرَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā waladī akhūka yakūnu sulṭāna dimashqa wa-anta sulṭānu baghdāda fa-shudda ʿazmaka wa-jahhiz amraka
sentences.l: And he said: O my son, your brother will be sultan of Damascus and you sultan of Baghdad; so tighten your resolve and prepare your affair.
sentences.i: He said, “My son, your brother shall be sultan of Damascus and you sultan of Baghdad. So steel your resolve and set your affairs in order.”

sentences.t: فَقَبِلَ مِنْهُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qabila minhu ḍawʾu al-makāni dhālika
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān accepted that from him.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān accepted his advice.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْحَاجِبَ قَدَّمَ إِلَيْهِ الْبَدْلَةَ الَّتِي كَانَتْ مَعَ الْوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ مِنْ مَلَابِسِ الْمُلُوكِ وَنَاوَلَهُ النِّمْشَةَ وَخَرَجَ مِنْ عِنْدِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-ḥājiba qaddama ilayhi al-badlata allatī kānat maʿa al-wazīri dandāna min malābisi al-mulūki wa-nāwalahu al-nimshata wa-kharaja min ʿindihi
sentences.l: Then the chamberlain presented to him the suit that had been with the vizier Dandān, of the garments of kings, and handed him the nimsha, and went out from his presence.
sentences.i: Then the chamberlain presented him with the suit of royal garments that had been with the vizier Dandān, and handed him the short sword, and went out from his presence.
sentences.n: النمشة is the Persian-derived nīmsha, a short sword or dagger; “suit” (بدلة) is the full set of robes. The reading “short sword” is the likeliest, since it is handed over after the robes of state.

sentences.t: وَأَمَرَ الْفَرَّاشِينَ أَنْ يَخْتَارُوا مَوْضِعاً عَالِياً وَيَنْصِبُوا فِيهِ خَيْمَةً وَاسِعَةً عَظِيمَةً لِلسُّلْطَانِ لِيَجْلِسَ فِيهَا إِذَا قَدِمَ عَلَيْهِ الْأُمَرَاءُ
sentences.tr: wa-amara al-farrāshīna an yakhtārū mawḍiʿan ʿāliyan wa-yanṣibū fīhi khaymatan wāsiʿatan ʿaẓīmatan li-al-sulṭāni li-yajlisa fīhā idhā qadima ʿalayhi al-umarāʾu
sentences.l: And he ordered the tent-pitchers to choose a high place and to pitch in it a tent wide and great for the sultan, that he sit in it when the emirs come to him.
sentences.i: He ordered the tent-pitchers to choose a high spot and pitch there a great, spacious tent for the sultan, where he could sit when the emirs came to him.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَمَرَ الطَّبَّاخِينَ أَنْ يَطْبُخُوا طَعَاماً فَاخِراً وَيُحْضِرُوهُ وَأَمَرَ السَّقَّائِينَ أَنْ يَنْصِبُوا حِيَاضَ الْمَاءِ
sentences.tr: thumma amara al-ṭabbākhīna an yaṭbukhū ṭaʿāman fākhiran wa-yuḥḍirūhu wa-amara al-saqqāʾīna an yanṣibū ḥiyāḍa al-māʾi
sentences.l: Then he ordered the cooks to cook food splendid and bring it, and ordered the water-carriers to set up the basins of water.
sentences.i: Then he ordered the cooks to prepare a splendid meal and bring it, and the water-carriers to set up basins of water.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ سَاعَةٍ طَارَ الْغُبَارُ حَتَّى سَدَّا لْأَقْطَارَ ثُمَّ انْكَشَفَ ذَلِكَ الْغُبَارُ وَبَانَ مِنْ تَحْتِهِ عَسْكَرٌ جَرَّارٌ مِثْلُ الْبَحْرِ الزَّخَّارِ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda sāʿatin ṭāra al-ghubāru ḥattā sadda al-aqṭāra thumma inkashafa dhālika al-ghubāru wa-bāna min taḥtihi ʿaskarun jarrārun mithlu al-baḥri al-zakhkhāri
sentences.l: And after an hour the dust flew up until it blocked the regions; then that dust was uncovered, and there appeared from beneath it an army, trailing, like the sea, surging.
sentences.i: After an hour a cloud of dust rose until it blocked out the horizons; then the dust lifted, and beneath it appeared a mighty army, like a surging sea.
sentences.n: The print divides سدّ الأقطار (“it blocked the regions”) as سدا لاقطار; it is read as two words, sadda al-aqṭāra. عسكر جرار, “a trailing army”, is the stock phrase for a vast host.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَ زَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَ—احِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahra zāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Then morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted tale unsaid.
sentences.n: The print has a dash inside المباح (“the permitted”) at the line end, probably a printer’s flaw; the word is the usual one in this closing formula.
